lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: A book with about 240 pages. Nobody on Earth can read it.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: It's called the Voynich manuscript. It is held at Yale's Beinecke Library. It's named for a book dealer who bought it in 1912.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Carbon dating in 2009 put the parchment between 1404 and 1438. That dates the material, not the writing.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: It's full of drawings. Plants no one can match to real ones. Circular charts of stars. Tiny figures bathing in green pools joined by pipes.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: The text uses an unknown alphabet of roughly 20 to 25 main characters. Around 38,000 words, about 8,000 to 9,000 different ones.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: It behaves like language. Word frequencies follow the same pattern as real languages. But it also has odd traits, like repeated words and a very predictable structure.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Theories: a cipher, an unknown language, an invented language, a hoax. Codebreakers from both world wars tried. None of the proposed solutions is accepted.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: It might say something. It might say nothing. Nobody has been able to prove which.
